note: Capture targets for step 1 of CAPTURE.md: thirty government screens, chosen because they are public, stable, and free of the copyright question. This file is INPUT. It is never written by capture_screens.mjs, and ids assigned here are the stable ids for the whole corpus — an id, once issued, is not reused or renumbered. The coverage flags (government, not_a_product, pre_2010) are capture-time claims; screen_type and every other judgement is left for annotation.

targets.licence_note: Open Government Licence v3.0 applies to gov.uk content. Captured for closed-module teaching use; not republished.
targets.why: The reference case for a government design system, and the one most students will already have seen.

targets.licence_note: Open Government Licence v3.0. Captured for closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: A service start page: one task, one action, almost no navigation. The counterpart to the polling-card theme in themes.json.

targets.licence_note: NHS website content, Open Government Licence v3.0 where stated. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: Health content for an anxious reader, and a different design system from GOV.UK in the same jurisdiction.

targets.licence_note: Open Parliament Licence v3.0. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: An institutional site rather than a service: hierarchy carrying prestige as well as information.

targets.licence_note: US federal government work, generally public domain. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: A federal portal whose job is routing rather than answering — the opposite structure to gov.uk.

targets.licence_note: US federal government work, generally public domain. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: Dense, obligation-carrying content — the money domain at its least friendly.

targets.licence_note: Crown copyright, Government of Canada; non-commercial reproduction terms. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: Half of a matched pair: the same design system, the same day, two languages.

targets.licence_note: Crown copyright, Government of Canada; non-commercial reproduction terms. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: The other half. French runs roughly 20% longer than English, so this pair shows what text expansion does to a layout that is otherwise identical.

targets.licence_note: Government of Ireland; Creative Commons or PSI licence where stated. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: A small-state portal that visibly borrows from GOV.UK — useful for asking what was copied and what was not.

targets.licence_note: Licence Ouverte / Open Licence (Etalab) where stated. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: France's citizen portal, and a design system (DSFR) with a published, legally mandated identity.

targets.licence_note: German federal government content; reuse terms per site notice. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: German compound nouns are the hardest realistic test of a fixed-width column and a button label.

targets.licence_note: Dutch government content, CC0 where stated. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: One of the longest-running government design systems in Europe, and unusually restrained.

targets.licence_note: Spanish government content; reuse per Ley 37/2007 notice on site. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: A portal built around administrative procedure rather than around the citizen's question.

targets.licence_note: Portuguese government content; reuse per site notice. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: A recent rebuild, so it shows current conventions rather than accumulated ones.

targets.licence_note: Swedish government content; reuse per site notice. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: Nordic government typography, and a site that leads with text rather than with cards.

targets.licence_note: Danish government content; reuse per site notice. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: A citizen portal in a country where nearly all public service is digital by default — the maturity case.

targets.licence_note: Finnish government content; reuse per site notice. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: Finnish word length is extreme even next to German, and the site is trilingual by statute. Captured at the Finnish front page: /frontpage redirects to the English version, which was the first capture and defeated the point of the target.

targets.licence_note: Estonian government content; reuse per site notice. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: The most-cited digital state, captured in English so the claim can be read rather than admired.

targets.licence_note: Greek government content; reuse per site notice. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: Greek script: a non-Latin alphabet that still sets in a Latin-style grid. gov.gr itself returns 403 to a headless browser, so the target moved to a Greek public body that does not, rather than recording a block as a screen.

targets.licence_note: Swiss Confederation content; reuse per site notice. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: Four national languages on one portal — the structural case for language choice as navigation.

targets.licence_note: © European Union; reuse under Decision 2011/833/EU where stated. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: A supranational body with 24 official languages, which is the hardest version of the problem gov.uk solves in one.

targets.licence_note: Japanese government content; reuse per site notice. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: Japanese sets without word spaces and breaks almost anywhere, which breaks the measure rule in principles.json rather than bending it.

targets.licence_note: Korean government content, KOGL where stated. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: Hangul at small sizes, and a portal far denser than any European example here.

targets.licence_note: HKSAR Government content; reuse per site notice. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: Traditional characters carry more strokes at the same point size, which is a legibility floor a Latin-trained eye does not predict.

targets.licence_note: Israeli government content; reuse per site notice. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: Right-to-left. Every assumption about where a page begins is reversed, including the direction of progress in a form. gov.il sits behind a Cloudflare challenge for headless browsers, so the RTL target moved to a body that answers.

targets.licence_note: UAE government content; reuse per site notice. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: The second right-to-left case, in a connected script, so RTL is not learned from a single example. The /ar-ae path used on the first pass returns 404.

targets.licence_note: Singapore Government content; reuse per site terms. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: English-language government design outside Europe and North America, with its own design system.

targets.licence_note: Government of India content; reuse per site notice. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: Devanagari, and a portal serving a scale no European example here approaches. india.gov.in returns 403 to a headless browser; the Hindi MyGov front page answers and carries the script, which was the reason for the target.

targets.licence_note: New Zealand Government content, CC BY 4.0 where stated. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: A bilingual English and te reo Maori portal, and a small-state site that chose plainness over identity.

targets.licence_note: Commonwealth of Australia, CC BY 4.0 where stated. Closed-module teaching use.
targets.why: Thirty is the round number the ordering in CAPTURE.md asks for, and this one closes the English-language set.
